candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina poster's SLAF-seq row: specific-locus amplified fragment sequencing for large-scale genotyping, depicted as an MseI/adaptor/AluI library route ending in amplified DNA. Sun et al. (2013) describes a matching common-carp implementation within the broader SLAF-seq method. The graph records the seven drawn transformations and a conceptual material boundary between initial digestion and adaptor attachment; it does not prescribe separate reactions. Neighboring ddRADseq, 2b-RAD and hyRAD rows, unshown enzyme schemes and application-specific adaptations are outside this extraction. The yellow genome highlight is unlabeled and is not taken as an affinity target or a defined chemical group.

features: Genomic-fragment-derived DNA is the sequenced carrier; insert sequence reports allelic variation at recovered SLAF loci.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven local operations belong to the explicitly labeled SLAF-seq row, with no alternative target or specimen branch drawn. The page-14 heading and matching captions establish that the supplied catalogue description applies. Sun et al.'s full text supports this particular MseI/adaptor/AluI route as its common-carp library implementation within SLAF-seq; the paper also uses other enzyme schemes in unshown pilot studies, so the row is not imposed on every SLAF-seq experiment. The double-barcode system and reduced-representation design clarify the information carried by the final DNA. Paper-reported length selection explains which genomic subset is represented; its unshown substeps are not inserted or assigned silently to the poster's Purify and pool caption. Application abstracts do not establish identical chemistry or additional target workflows.
